answers.q: All the readings in the whole field are wrong, fix them.
answers.a:
I cannot fix the readings as I do not have access to well data or the ability to modify records. However, I can provide information related to spills and safety protocols.

A maintenance report (MNT-0001-029) from June 11, 2026, details a crude oil spill of an estimated 6.8 bbl around a flowline coupling, staining 9.4% of the pad. This was a reportable spill and required immediate shut-in according to the T200 manual. The well was shut in by Jake Morales on the afternoon of June 11, 2026. The spill was contained approximately 7 hours after the inspection flight. The spill report to the State Oil & Gas Commission was filed 41 hours after detection on June 13, 2026, due to a missed HSE on-call handover. The root cause was external corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the threaded coupling.

Regarding safety protocols, the field-work-sop manual outlines several procedures:
*   **WS-06** (fleet/sops/field-work-sop.md) states that contaminated soil, absorbents, and replaced parts with oil on them are waste and must be bagged, contained, and shipped with a waste manifest to an approved disposal site.
*   **WS-03** (fleet/sops/field-work-sop.md) requires every crew member to wear a personal H2S monitor, bump-tested daily. Work must stop if any monitor reads 10 ppm or more, and personnel must move upwind and not return until readings are below 10 ppm and approved by the HSE officer. This 10 ppm action level is also mentioned in API RP 49 (fleet/sops/field-work-sop.md).
*   The spill-response-sop (fleet/sops/spill-response-sop.md) indicates that our company's reporting threshold for crude oil losses is 5 bbl or more, and a written report is required within 24 hours. Cleanup standards, such as those in Texas Statewide Rule 91, require free oil removal and soil cleaned to 1.0% total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) by weight.
Assumed: Assuming 'readings' refers to general data and 'fix them' implies a need for information on data correction, the best default is to search documentation for relevant procedures.

answers.q: What temperature rise above air means WELL-0007 is producing, and where does that rule come from?
answers.a: WELL-0007 is a T350 well. A T350 well is considered producing when its wellhead temperature is at least 20 °C above the ambient air temperature at the time of the reading (fleet/well-types/T350.md). This rule comes from section 3 of the T350 well type manual (fleet/well-types/T350.md).

answers.q: What temperature rise above air means WELL-0001 is producing, and where does that rule come from?
answers.a: A T200 well, such as WELL-0001, is considered producing when its wellhead temperature is at least 15 °C above the ambient air temperature at the time of the reading (fleet/well-types/T200.md). This rule is found in section 9.3, "Production temperature rule," of the T200 manual (fleet/well-types/T200.md). A difference below 15 °C means the well is not producing for that reading (fleet/well-types/T200.md). For example, during inspection INS-0001-0140, WELL-0001's wellhead temperature was 8.5 °C above air temperature, indicating it was not producing (MNT-0001-021).
